Fixed by flock-based staging liveness in dylib_cache.rs (commit 0fdd3bd3). A compile holds an exclusive advisory flock on a sibling <artifact-id>.tmp.lock from before the staging dir exists until it is renamed/cleaned; the sweep only deletes staging whose lock it can acquire (or whose lock file is gone), with fd/path inode re-verification closing the create-vs-unlink race. Not needed on current evidence: modern Linux targets run PipeWire, so cpal's ALSA backend already routes through pipewire-alsa and gets PipeWire's low-latency scheduling — JACK's historical advantage is absorbed (PipeWire is also the JACK server on these systems). With RT promotion handled by eseq-linux.53/.54/.58, the remaining latency lever is buffer/period size on the existing ALSA path (e.g. PIPEWIRE_LATENCY), not a host switch, and cpal's jack feature would add a system dependency plus host-selection complexity for a second-class backend. REOPEN TRIGGER: if eseq-linux.12's latency/perf validation measures the ALSA-via-PipeWire path failing the frame/latency budget at reasonable buffer sizes, recreate or reopen this.
